package.title: What Happens If You Quit Sugar for 30 Days
package.phrase: what happens if you quit sugar for 30 days
package.opener: What happens if you quit sugar for 30 days? Little evidence says sugar is addictive in people, so the cravings are not a drug withdrawal. Juice, honey and syrups still count as free sugar; the WHO's limit is under 10% of daily energy, about 12 teaspoons for someone eating about 2,000 calories, and caries are lower below it. In a 9-day study of children with obesity, swapping sugar for starch at the same calories nearly halved liver fat (7.2% to 3.8%). The WHO advises not to swap sugar for sweeteners. In trials of adults, eating less sugar took off about 0.8 kg, because people ate fewer calories. And in one small trial, after three months on less sugar, sweet foods tasted about 40% sweeter.

sources.label: World Health Organization. Healthy diet (fact sheet)
sources.note: 'free sugars should be limited to less than 10% of total daily energy intake, which is equivalent to 50 g (or about 12 level teaspoons) for a person of healthy body weight consuming about 2000 calories per day'; free sugars include sugars 'added to foods and beverages by the manufacturer, cook or consumer, and sugars naturally present in honey, syrups, fruit juices and fruit juice concentrates'; 'Reducing consumption of free sugars ... should be accomplished without the use of non-sugar sweeteners.'

sources.label: Te Morenga L, Mallard S, Mann J. Dietary sugars and body weight: systematic review and meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials and cohort studies. BMJ 2013;346:e7492
sources.note: 'In trials of adults with ad libitum diets ... reduced intake of dietary sugars was associated with a decrease in body weight (0.80 kg, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.21)'; 'Isoenergetic exchange of dietary sugars with other carbohydrates showed no change in body weight'; the change 'seems to be mediated via changes in energy intakes'. The video rounds 0.8 kg to 'about one kilo'.

sources.label: Schwarz JM et al. Effects of dietary fructose restriction on liver fat, de novo lipogenesis, and insulin kinetics in children with obesity. Gastroenterology 2017;153:743-52
sources.note: 41 children aged 9-18 with obesity, 9 days, the same calories with starch in place of sugar: 'liver fat decreased from a median of 7.2% ... to 3.8%'; 'insulin kinetics improved'.

sources.label: Wise PM, Nattress L, Flammer LJ, Beauchamp GK. Reduced dietary intake of simple sugars alters perceived sweet taste intensity but not perceived pleasantness. Am J Clin Nutr 2016;103:50-60
sources.note: Low-sugar group 16 (13 completed key parts), control 17: 'no systematic differences ... during the baseline or first diet month'; 'During the third diet month, the low-sugar subjects rated both low and high concentrations in puddings as ∼40% sweeter than did the control group'. One small trial; two authors worked at PepsiCo (declared).

sources.label: Westwater ML, Fletcher PC, Ziauddeen H. Sugar addiction: the state of the science. Eur J Nutr 2016;55(Suppl 2):55-69
sources.note: 'We find little evidence to support sugar addiction in humans'. No conflicts.

sources.label: Moynihan PJ, Kelly SA. Effect on caries of restricting sugars intake: systematic review to inform WHO guidelines. J Dent Res 2014;93:8-18
sources.note: 55 studies; 'evidence of moderate quality showing that caries is lower when free-sugars intake is < 10% E'.

lines.text: And me? Sweet food tastes just the same.
No sugar for a month? Not yet. Three months? Forty percent sweeter!

cta.text: Quitting sugar: know this. Juice and honey count as sugar too. Don't swap sugar for sweeteners. Keep it under twelve teaspoons a day. Follow MedPeak Health for more health tips that keep you safe.

musicPrompt: A steady, continuous playful cartoon caper groove at 104 BPM that never stops or drops out: a constant tight drum beat, a bouncy plucked bass line and a held warm organ pad under everything from the first second to the last, no breaks, no silences, no stop-time stabs. A sneaky pizzicato and clarinet melody on top, mischievous like a villain tiptoeing, with a bright triumphant brass lift near the end. Background music under dialogue.
